title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with competition and collaborations, as companies vie for attention and funding. Notable developments include new lunar navigation efforts and a flurry of activity around satellite cancellations and launches.

themes.title: Competition Heats Up
themes.body: Rocketeers are making their mark at the IREC, showcasing innovations and vying for investor interest. Meanwhile, SpaceX's upcoming Starship version 3 launch adds fuel to the competitive fire.

themes.title: Lunar Navigation Ventures
themes.body: Northrop Grumman is setting its sights on the lunar navigation market with a Webb-derived guidance system, indicating a strategic pivot towards lunar operations. This move could position them well as lunar missions ramp up.

themes.title: Satellite Cancellations Continue
themes.body: SES and Eutelsat's decision to cancel GEO expansion satellites highlights the ongoing challenges in the satellite market. As operators reassess their strategies, the implications for future satellite deployments remain uncertain.

themes.title: Funding and Collaborations
themes.body: Varda's partnership with United Therapeutics for microgravity drug research exemplifies the growing interest in space-based applications. Additionally, Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program signals robust demand for ground station capabilities.
